title: LGMT: Metamorphic Testing Tool Exposes Up to 29.44% Logical Inconsistencies in LLMs
tldr: LGMT is an open-source tool designed to evaluate the logical reasoning reliability of LLMs using metamorphic testing grounded in first-order logic. By generating logically equivalent variants of premise-conclusion pairs without needing ground-truth labels, LGMT checks for internal logical contradictions across model outputs. Empirical evaluation across six popular LLMs on 3,091 metamorphic groups revealed inconsistency rates between 20.84% and 29.44%.
takeaways: Utilizes 20 built-in metamorphic relations grounded in first-order logic and supports custom relations verified via the Z3 theorem prover.
Evaluates LLM logical entailment predictions without requiring ground-truth labels by checking consistency across transformed follow-up test cases.
Revealed high logical inconsistency rates (20.84% to 29.44%) across six leading LLMs evaluated on 3,091 metamorphic test groups.
code:
# Pseudocode illustration of LGMT execution flow
from lgmt import MetamorphicTester, Z3Verifier

tester = MetamorphicTester(model_id="gpt-4o", offline_mode=False)
relation = tester.load_relation("contraposition")
assert Z3Verifier.verify(relation.logic_formula)

source_case = {"premise": "If P then Q. P is True.", "conclusion": "Q is True."}
followup_case = relation.transform(source_case)

inconsistent = tester.check_consistency(source_case, followup_case)
fullAnalysis: Large Language Models are increasingly integrated into modern software systems as reasoning components, yet static benchmarks evaluate queries in isolation and fail to expose internal contradictions. LGMT addresses this limitation by introducing metamorphic testing grounded in first-order logic for LLMs. Given a source test case in premise-conclusion form, LGMT generates logically equivalent follow-up test cases and checks whether the model's entailment predictions remain consistent across the pair, operating completely without ground-truth labels.\n\nThe framework features 20 built-in metamorphic relations, supports user-defined custom relations verified by the Z3 theorem prover, and includes CLI, web studio, and offline mock execution modes. Across six widely used LLMs evaluated on a bundled benchmark of 3,091 metamorphic groups, LGMT uncovered logical inconsistency rates ranging from 20.84% to 29.44%, highlighting significant reliability risks when deploying LLMs for logical reasoning tasks.
